native_result.query: In which years were individuals with a criminal record found to have significantly lower wealth compared to those without?
native_result.HypoA: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
native_result.HypoB: In the supplied NLSY79-derived dataset, individuals ever jailed between 1985 and 1994 held significantly lower composite wealth than those never jailed in both 1990 and 1996 (Holm-adjusted p<1e-12 for Welch's t and Mann-Whitney; Hedges' g=-0.27 and g=-0.44; HC3-robust OLS coefficient on ever_jailed negative and CI excludes zero after race/sex adjustment). The same direction also holds at 1985 (Welch p=7.3e-19, g=-0.31), but 1985 is the start of the jail-exposure window and is reported as a pre-period baseline check, not as a causal effect.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows x 6 cols, no missing). For each wealth year (1985, 1990, 1996): (a) computed descriptive stats by ever_jailed; (b) applied per-year shift-log transform log(wealth - min(wealth) + 1) to handle 358-649 negative-wealth observations; (c) Welch's t-test on the log-shift wealth (recomputed two-sided p via t.sf since scipy underflowed to 0.0); (d) Mann-Whitney U on raw wealth as a non-parametric backup (p via normal-approx); (e) HC3-robust OLS of log-shift wealth on ever_jailed + C(race) + C(sex); (f) Holm-Bonferroni-adjusted p-values across the 3 year-wise tests; (g) declared a year "significantly lower" only if (Holm-adjusted p<0.05 on Welch or MW) AND (|Hedges' g on log shift|>=0.20 OR |rank-biserial r|>=0.10) AND direction was negative (jailed < never-jailed). 1985 framed as pre-period baseline per researcher instruction.

sub_hypo.text: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.
sub_hypo.context: Participants in the National Longitudinal Study of Youth's 1979 cohort, with wealth measured in 1985, 1990, and 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Individuals jailed between 1985 and 1994 (ever_jailed = 1) have significantly lower composite wealth in each of 1985, 1990, and 1996 than individuals not jailed during that period (ever_jailed = 0).

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In 1985, 1990, and 1996, individuals with a criminal record have significantly lower wealth compared to those without.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals ever jailed between 1985 and 1994 held significantly lower composite wealth in 1990 than those never jailed, including after adjustment for race and sex.
sub_hypo.context: The supplied NLSY79-derived dataset of 12,013 participants with no missing data; jail exposure defined over 1985–1994 and wealth measured in 1990.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed participants had lower wealth: Holm-adjusted p<1e-12 for both Welch's t-test on log(wealth - min(wealth) + 1) and Mann-Whitney U on raw wealth; Hedges' g=-0.27 on log-shift wealth. HC3-robust OLS of log-shift wealth adjusting for categorical race and sex yielded a negative ever_jailed coefficient with a confidence interval excluding zero. Holm adjustment covered the three wealth-year tests. Significantly lower required adjusted p<0.05 on Welch or Mann-Whitney, |g|>=0.20 or |rank-biserial r|>=0.10, and a negative direction.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals ever jailed between 1985 and 1994 held significantly lower composite wealth in 1996 than those never jailed, including after adjustment for race and sex.
sub_hypo.context: The supplied NLSY79-derived dataset of 12,013 participants with no missing data; jail exposure defined over 1985–1994 and wealth measured in 1996.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed participants had lower wealth: Holm-adjusted p<1e-12 for both Welch's t-test on log(wealth - min(wealth) + 1) and Mann-Whitney U on raw wealth; Hedges' g=-0.44 on log-shift wealth. HC3-robust OLS of log-shift wealth adjusting for categorical race and sex yielded a negative ever_jailed coefficient with a confidence interval excluding zero. Holm adjustment covered the three wealth-year tests. Significantly lower required adjusted p<0.05 on Welch or Mann-Whitney, |g|>=0.20 or |rank-biserial r|>=0.10, and a negative direction.

sub_hypo.text: Individuals ever jailed between 1985 and 1994 also held lower composite wealth in 1985 than those never jailed; this is a pre-period baseline check, not a causal effect.
sub_hypo.context: The supplied NLSY79-derived dataset of 12,013 participants with no missing data; 1985 is the start of the 1985–1994 jail-exposure window and is treated as a pre-period baseline.
sub_hypo.relations: Jailed participants had lower baseline wealth, with Welch p=7.3e-19 and Hedges' g=-0.31 on per-year log-shift wealth, log(wealth - min(wealth) + 1). This negative association is not interpreted as a causal effect.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In the supplied NLSY79-derived dataset, individuals ever jailed between 1985 and 1994 held significantly lower composite wealth than those never jailed in both 1990 and 1996 (Holm-adjusted p<1e-12 for Welch's t and Mann-Whitney; Hedges' g=-0.27 and g=-0.44; HC3-robust OLS coefficient on ever_jailed negative and CI excludes zero after race/sex adjustment). The same direction also holds at 1985 (Welch p=7.3e-19, g=-0.31), but 1985 is the start of the jail-exposure window and is reported as a pre-period baseline check, not as a causal effect.
